Every control is optional. Drag a slider or tap a picture to compare, tap what you want, press Copy answers, paste the line to jep.

Your ruling, 15 Nov: "A sounds good." Your note on the Yuppie: "Regarding the Yuppie: no execution looks good. Can't hold 3 things (suitcase, phone, cigar) at once. Can't have suspenders above jacket - in fact, shouldn't have a jacket at all."

What was done on your ruling, and what it showed

  1. Built: film_finish.py, one recipe per decade for nine decades. It runs on the processor with no image model in memory: 3 seconds for these nine pictures. The output keeps the picture's size, which is what lets the slider below fade it over the original.
  2. Blind test: a critic who never saw the code dated every photograph before learning its target decade, with originals and finished versions shuffled together. Originals dated to their own decade: 3 of 9. Finished: 7 of 9 (misses: 1950s read as 1960s, 1960s read as 1970s).
  3. Period feel, 1 to 5, same critic: 2.33 for the originals, 3.67 finished.
  4. The risk named when you ruled, that a weak recipe reads as a phone filter: the critic judged the ageing "laid on afterwards" in 4 of 9 finished pictures, was unsure on 3, and said no on 2.
  5. The cost: the same critic's look score went from 4.00 to 3.22. The finish trades polish for period; whether that trade lifts your own score is what the taps below measure.
  6. One tuning pass on a first critic's notes (finer grain, thinner dust, print borders left as clean paper) did not raise the scores. First recipes, first critic: dated right 7 of 9, period 2.00 to 3.89, laid on in 2 of 9, look 4.00 to 3.67. Two judges differ by about this much, so read the two rounds as agreeing: the finish dates the photograph, costs some polish, and its grain is the part that still reads as an overlay.
  7. Your T7 answers are applied to what is shown: the 1920s cloth tuxedo, the 2010s denim jacket, the radio waist-up, the yarn ball full figure. The 2000s has no head yet and the Yuppie has no picture you accept; both are staged in Part 2.
